incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency SLO burn detected in us-west-2 inference cluster for model redwood-13b-v2. p95=480ms p99=2.3s sustained >5m. PagerDuty incident PDX-8921 created. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-tail

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty PDX-8921 routed to eng-oncall rotation (primary: alice chen). PagerDuty link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PDX-8921 :bell:

alice chen: acking PD. I'm on it. First check: autoscaler + recent deploys.

samir patel: I'm here, +1. Seeing spike in concurrent small requests to /generate, KV cache hit-rate dropped to ~12% which could explain tail.

maria gomez: Any deployment around 11:15-11:25 UTC? I see a canary for quantized runtime (q8) started ~11:18. Could be regression on quantized kernel.

alice chen: yep, canary rolled at 11:18 to 10% traffic. I'll check rollout and hold if needed.

evan k: pulling tail traces now. Quick command I ran:```sh
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/series?metric=latency.p99&env=us-west-2&model=redwood-13b-v2&window=10m" | jq .
```
Output shows p99 spike aligned with canary start.

samir patel: propose emergency mitigation: divert traffic off canary and/or route to fallback model variant, and scale up inference pool by +4 nodes while we investigate. That should buy time to warm KV cache.

alice chen: doing both. Scaling now and routing 100% to fallback variant. Commands below:```bash
# scale up pool
rictl capacity scale --pool inference-usw2 --add 4 --reason "p99 burn emergency"
# route traffic to fallback model variant
rictl routing update --route /generate --model redwood-13b-v2-fallback --weight 100 --timeout 30s
# rollback canary
rictl rollout set --canary-id canary-2026-03-15 --pct 0
```

incident-bot: Autoscaler action queued: adding 4 nodes to inference-usw2. Expected ready in ~90-150s. Routing change applied. :gear:

maria gomez: after routing change p99 dropped from 2.3s -> ~820ms within 70s, p95 at ~380ms and KV hit-rate climbing to 44%. Good sign.

alice chen: confirmed canary set to 0%. Leaving fallback in place while we monitor. Also added temporary rate-limit to high-concurrency path for a further 10% reduction of tail.

samir patel: I pushed a short-lived suppression to PagerDuty to avoid duplicate noisy pages: pd-suppress PDX-8921 12m by alice chen. :white_check_mark:

evan k: Customer-impact-bot summary (auto): "~0.8% of requests in the 12:10-12:20 window experienced >2s latency. No 5xx errors observed. Top affected tenants: AcmeCorp (0.3% requests), BetaApps (0.1%). User-visible slowdown reported by internal telemetry for high-concurrency clients." Adding to incident ticket.

lenora (oncall): I'm the next shift, will take handoff in ~18m. Documenting actions: scaled +4 nodes, rolled canary to 0, routed to fallback variant, rate-limited /generate hotpath, suppression set. I'll watch health checks and kv hit rate. Anything else to add before my takeover? :memo:

maria gomez: pls run KV pre-warm for top hotkeys and recheck coldstart metrics. Quick helper:```py
# prewarm script (run on one worker)
from redis import Redis
keys = get_top_hotkeys(200)
r = Redis.from_url("redis://kv-cache:6379")
for k in keys:
    r.get(k)
```
I've kicked this off. KV hit-rate now 76% and p95 trending to 210ms.

alice chen: verified pre-warm started and completed for prioritized hotkeys. Observed decreased tail on hosts with warmed caches. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident PDX-8921 status updated: acknowledged -> mitigated (awaiting verification window). Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PDX-8921

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Current: p99 <= SLO (now ~220ms), p95 ~200ms and stable for 2min. Suggested action: keep incident open 30m for verification, then close if stable.

lenora (oncall): I'll keep it open and monitor 30m. I'll post final postmortem checklist items in ticket (deploy review, quantized kernel regression test, improve canary isolation). Taking responsibility for follow-up. Thanks team. :pray:

customer-impact-bot: Notifying account execs for AcmeCorp with brief: "We experienced brief latency degradation affecting a small subset of requests between 12:10-12:20 UTC; mitigation applied and system is stable. Follow-up with timeline to come."

alice chen: adding notes to runbook and incident ticket. Good job all, will hand over to lenora in 15m. :coffee:
